questions.stem: A map on which the scale is shown as 1:50,000 is using
questions.explanation: 1:50,000 (or 1/50,000) is the representative fraction (R.F.) form of scale.

questions.stem: On a map of scale 1:50,000, a road measuring 4 cm represents a ground distance of
The statement scale '2 cm represents 1 km' expressed as a representative fraction is
On a map of scale 1:25,000, the distance between two villages is 6.4 cm. The actual distance is
A rectangular forest reserve measures 3 cm by 2 cm on a map of scale 1:50,000. Its actual area is
questions.explanation: 3 cm = 1.5 km and 2 cm = 1 km, so area = 1.5 x 1 = 1.5 km2.

questions.stem: A map that shows the boundaries of individual plots of land and buildings for ownership and taxation is
questions.explanation: Cadastral maps record land ownership and property boundaries.

questions.stem: On a topographical map, contour lines that are very close together indicate
questions.explanation: Closely spaced contours mean a large change of height over a short distance.

questions.stem: Two points on a map are at 400 m and 150 m above sea level and are 5 km apart horizontally. The average gradient between them is
questions.explanation: Vertical interval 250 m over 5,000 m: 5,000/250 = 20, so 1 in 20.

questions.stem: On a contour map, a series of V-shaped contours with the V pointing towards higher ground indicates
questions.explanation: Contour Vs point upstream (towards higher land) in a valley; on a spur they point towards lower ground.

questions.stem: The forward bearing of a hill from a school is 060 degrees. The back bearing of the school from the hill is
questions.explanation: Back bearing = forward bearing + 180 = 240 degrees.

questions.stem: GIS stands for
questions.explanation: A Geographic Information System captures, stores, analyses and displays spatial data.

questions.stem: A school is setting up a GIS laboratory. Which of the following items is NOT a component of a GIS?
questions.explanation: GIS components are hardware, software, data, people and methods; a rain gauge is a weather instrument.

questions.stem: In GIS, data stored as a grid of cells (pixels), such as a satellite image, is called
questions.explanation: Raster data uses cells; vector data uses points, lines and polygons.

questions.stem: In a vector GIS, a road network would normally be represented as
questions.explanation: Linear features such as roads and rivers are stored as lines.

questions.stem: The acquisition of information about the earth's surface from satellites or aircraft without physical contact is
questions.explanation: Remote sensing supplies much of the data used in GIS.

questions.stem: A state government wants to choose the best site for a new hospital using maps of population, roads and existing health centres. GIS would help mainly by
options: overlaying the different data layers to identify suitable locations
replacing the need for any data
questions.explanation: Overlay analysis combines layers to support site selection and planning.

questions.stem: A map that shows population density by shading areas in different intensities of colour is
questions.explanation: Choropleth maps shade administrative areas according to value ranges.

questions.stem: Lines joining places with equal amounts of rainfall are called
questions.explanation: Isohyets link equal rainfall; isotherms equal temperature; isobars equal pressure; isohels equal sunshine.

questions.stem: In a pie chart showing a state's exports totalling ₦4,800 million, cocoa worth ₦1,200 million should be represented by a sector of
Which statistical diagram is most suitable for showing the volume of goods moving along different routes?
questions.explanation: Flow maps use lines of proportional width to show movement.

questions.stem: A sector representing 35 per cent of a total in a pie chart has an angle of
questions.explanation: 0.35 x 360 = 126 degrees.

questions.stem: The main disadvantage of a dot map is that
options: dots may merge in densely populated areas, making counting difficult
it can show only one country
questions.explanation: In crowded areas dots coalesce, so values are hard to read.

questions.stem: Proportional circles are used on a map to show
options: quantities at specific places, such as town populations
questions.explanation: The area of each circle is proportional to the value it represents.

questions.stem: In which direction does the earth spin on its axis?
questions.explanation: Rotation from west to east makes the sun appear to rise in the east.

questions.stem: The rotation of the earth causes
options: the varying length of the year
questions.explanation: Seasons result from revolution with an inclined axis.

questions.stem: The overhead (vertical) noon sun is at the Tropic of Cancer on about
questions.explanation: 21 June is the summer solstice in the northern hemisphere.

questions.stem: Days and nights are equal all over the world on
questions.explanation: At the equinoxes the sun is overhead at the equator.

questions.stem: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich (0 degrees), the local time at a place on longitude 45 degrees E is
questions.explanation: 45 x 4 minutes = 3 hours ahead, so 3.00 p.m.

questions.stem: It is 9.00 a.m. at a town on longitude 30 degrees W. The local time at a town on longitude 15 degrees E is
questions.explanation: Difference = 45 degrees = 3 hours; the eastern town is ahead: 12.00 noon.

questions.stem: A football match starts at 2.00 p.m. local time in a city on longitude 60 degrees E. The local time in a city on longitude 30 degrees W when the match starts is
questions.explanation: Difference = 90 degrees = 6 hours; west is behind: 2.00 p.m. - 6 h = 8.00 a.m.

questions.stem: The local time at a place is 2 hours 40 minutes behind Greenwich. The longitude of the place is
questions.explanation: 160 minutes / 4 = 40 degrees; behind Greenwich means west.

questions.stem: A traveller crossing the International Date Line from west to east (from Asia towards America) should
options: put the calendar back by one day
put the calendar forward by one day
add one hour to the watch
make no change to the date
questions.explanation: Travelling eastward across the line, the same date is repeated.

questions.stem: Using 111 km for one degree of latitude, the distance along a meridian between latitudes 5 degrees N and 12 degrees N is about
questions.explanation: 7 degrees x 111 km = 777 km.

questions.stem: The angle of the noon sun at latitude 10 degrees N on 21 June is
questions.explanation: The sun is overhead at 23.5 N; 23.5 - 10 = 13.5; 90 - 13.5 = 76.5 degrees.

questions.stem: Which of the following is evidence that the earth is spherical?
options: The circular shadow of the earth on the moon during a lunar eclipse
questions.explanation: Only a sphere casts a circular shadow from every angle.

questions.stem: The planet nearest to the sun is
questions.explanation: Mercury is the innermost planet of the solar system.

questions.stem: The earth is nearest to the sun (perihelion) in
questions.explanation: Perihelion is about 3 January; aphelion about 4 July.

questions.stem: The Arctic Circle experiences 24 hours of daylight on about 21 June mainly because
options: the North Pole is tilted towards the sun
the earth is nearest to the sun
the sun is overhead at the equator
questions.explanation: The axial tilt of about 23.5 degrees keeps the area north of the Arctic Circle in sunlight.

questions.stem: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma are
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form from magma or lava.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an extrusive igneous rock?
questions.explanation: Basalt forms from lava cooling quickly at the surface; granite cools slowly underground.

questions.stem: When limestone is subjected to great heat and pressure it changes into
questions.explanation: Limestone becomes marble; shale becomes slate; sandstone becomes quartzite.

questions.stem: Coal is classified as
options: a metamorphic rock formed from granite
questions.explanation: Coal forms from compressed plant remains.

questions.stem: Sedimentary rocks are usually
questions.explanation: Layers (strata) and fossils are typical of sedimentary rocks.

questions.stem: The large crystals found in granite indicate that it
options: cooled slowly deep inside the earth
questions.explanation: Slow cooling allows large crystals to form.

questions.stem: Shale subjected to pressure during mountain building changes into
questions.explanation: Shale metamorphoses to slate.

questions.stem: Limestone quarried at Ewekoro in Ogun State is used mainly for
questions.explanation: Limestone is the main raw material for cement manufacture, e.g. in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Rocks formed from the accumulation of shells and skeletons of marine organisms include
questions.explanation: These are organically formed calcareous sedimentary rocks.

questions.stem: Sandstone metamorphoses into
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure recrystallise the quartz grains into quartzite.

questions.stem: The point on the earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake is the
questions.explanation: The focus is underground; the epicentre is vertically above it.

questions.stem: The instrument used to record earthquake waves is the
questions.explanation: Seismographs record seismic waves.

questions.stem: An upfold of rock layers produced by compression is
questions.explanation: Anticlines are arch-shaped upfolds; synclines are downfolds.

questions.stem: A rift valley is formed when
options: a river cuts down through soft rock
a block of land sinks between two roughly parallel faults
questions.explanation: Rift valleys (graben) form by faulting.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a fold mountain?
questions.explanation: The Atlas are fold mountains; the Vosges and Ruwenzori are block mountains; Mount Cameroon is volcanic.

questions.stem: A block mountain (horst) is formed when
options: lava piles up around a vent
a block of land is uplifted between two faults or the land on either side sinks
questions.explanation: Horsts are fault-bounded uplands.

questions.stem: Mount Cameroon, close to Nigeria's eastern border, is
questions.explanation: Mount Cameroon is one of Africa's most active volcanoes.

questions.stem: Molten rock that cools in a vertical crack cutting across rock layers forms
questions.explanation: Dykes are vertical, discordant intrusions; sills are horizontal, concordant.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a positive effect of volcanic activity?
questions.explanation: Volcanic soils are fertile; volcanic areas may also have geothermal energy and minerals.

questions.stem: The theory that the continents were once joined together in a single land mass and have drifted apart refers to the land mass called
questions.explanation: Wegener's continental drift theory proposed the supercontinent Pangaea.

questions.stem: The breakdown of rocks in situ (in their original position) is called
questions.explanation: Weathering does not involve movement; erosion does.

questions.stem: Exfoliation is a type of
options: mechanical weathering caused by alternate heating and cooling
questions.explanation: Outer layers of rock peel off due to temperature changes, common in deserts.

questions.stem: The chemical weathering of limestone by rainwater containing carbon dioxide is
questions.explanation: Carbonic acid dissolves calcium carbonate.

questions.stem: An ox-bow lake is formed in the
questions.explanation: Ox-bow lakes form when meanders are cut off on a flood plain.

questions.stem: A V-shaped valley is a feature of
options: river erosion in the youthful stage
questions.explanation: Vertical erosion in the upper course produces V-shaped valleys; glaciers produce U-shaped valleys.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a depositional feature of a river?
questions.explanation: Levees are raised banks built by deposition during floods.

questions.stem: A crescent-shaped sand dune with horns pointing downwind is
questions.explanation: Barchans form where wind blows mainly from one direction.

questions.stem: A rock pedestal (mushroom rock) in deserts is formed mainly by
questions.explanation: Sand-laden wind erodes most strongly near the base.

questions.stem: An armchair-shaped hollow on a mountainside formed by glacial erosion is
questions.explanation: Cirques (corries) are erosional; moraines, drumlins and eskers are depositional.

questions.stem: A narrow ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and extending into the sea is
questions.explanation: Spits form by longshore drift.

questions.stem: A sand bar joining an island to the mainland is called
questions.explanation: Tombolos form by deposition between an island and the coast.

questions.stem: In limestone caves, an icicle-shaped deposit hanging from the roof is
questions.explanation: Stalactites hang from the roof; stalagmites grow up from the floor.

questions.stem: The downslope movement of rock and soil under the influence of gravity is known as
questions.explanation: Mass wasting includes soil creep, landslides and mudflows.

questions.stem: A waterfall is most likely to form where
options: a river meanders on a flood plain
a band of hard rock lies across a river's course above softer rock
questions.explanation: Softer rock downstream is eroded faster, creating a sharp drop.

questions.stem: The instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure is the
questions.explanation: Barometers measure pressure; anemometers measure wind speed.

questions.stem: Wind direction is shown by the
questions.explanation: A wind vane points to the direction from which wind blows.

questions.stem: A wet-and-dry bulb thermometer (hygrometer) is used to determine
questions.explanation: The difference between the two readings gives relative humidity.

questions.stem: Air at a certain temperature contains 12 g of water vapour per cubic metre but could hold 20 g. Its relative humidity is
questions.explanation: 12/20 x 100 = 60 per cent.

questions.stem: The Stevenson screen is painted white mainly to
questions.explanation: White reflects radiation so instruments record shade air temperature.

questions.stem: Rainfall that occurs when moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier is
questions.explanation: The windward side is wet; the leeward side lies in a rain shadow.

questions.stem: Dark, towering clouds associated with thunderstorms and heavy rain are
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds have great vertical development.

questions.stem: If the temperature at sea level is 28 degrees C, the temperature at the top of a mountain 2,000 m high, using a normal lapse rate of 6.5 degrees C per 1,000 m, is
questions.explanation: 28 - (6.5 x 2) = 15 degrees C.

questions.stem: A town at 200 m above sea level records 30 degrees C. Using a lapse rate of 6.5 degrees C per 1,000 m, the expected temperature at a place 1,400 m above sea level is
questions.explanation: Height difference 1,200 m: 6.5 x 1.2 = 7.8; 30 - 7.8 = 22.2 degrees C.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why convectional rainfall is common in the afternoon in equatorial regions?
options: Cold air from the poles reaches the equator at noon
Mountains force air to rise in the afternoon
The sea becomes warmer than the land at night
Intense morning heating causes moist air to rise, cool and condense
questions.explanation: Strong heating builds cumulonimbus clouds by afternoon.

questions.stem: Lines on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure are
questions.explanation: Isobars show pressure patterns and wind systems.

questions.stem: Land breezes blow from land to sea at night because
options: the sea is cooler than the land at night
the land cools faster than the sea, creating higher pressure over the land
the moon attracts air towards the sea
questions.explanation: Air moves from high pressure over cooler land to lower pressure over the warmer sea.

questions.stem: Rainfall, temperature, humidity and wind are described as
questions.explanation: Elements are rainfall, temperature, humidity, pressure, wind and sunshine; latitude, altitude and ocean currents are factors.

questions.stem: Using the monthly temperatures 27, 28, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 24, 25, 26, 27, 27 degrees C, the annual range of temperature is
questions.explanation: 28 - 24 = 4 degrees C.

questions.stem: For the same monthly temperatures (27, 28, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 24, 25, 26, 27, 27 degrees C), the mean annual temperature is about
questions.explanation: Sum 314 / 12 = 26.2 degrees C.

questions.stem: A warm ocean current flowing along a coast generally
options: raises the temperature and increases rainfall of the coastal lands
lowers coastal temperatures and causes fog only
questions.explanation: Warm currents warm the air and add moisture; cold currents (e.g. Benguela) favour deserts.

questions.stem: Places near the sea have a smaller annual range of temperature than inland places because
options: water heats and cools more slowly than land
there is no wind at the coast
questions.explanation: This is the moderating (maritime) influence of the sea.

questions.stem: A climate with hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters is the
questions.explanation: Winter rainfall is the distinctive feature of the Mediterranean climate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of the equatorial climate?
options: A long dry season with very cold winters
Heavy rainfall throughout the year and a small annual range of temperature
questions.explanation: Equatorial regions have no true dry season and temperatures of about 27 degrees C all year.

questions.stem: Hot deserts such as the Namib and the Atacama are found mainly on the
options: western sides of continents between about 15 and 30 degrees of latitude
eastern sides of continents near the equator
questions.explanation: Descending air of the subtropical high and cold currents cause aridity.

questions.stem: In Koppen's classification, climates are grouped mainly on the basis of
options: temperature and rainfall and their effect on natural vegetation
questions.explanation: Koppen used temperature and precipitation values linked to vegetation.

questions.stem: The tropical continental (Sudan) type of climate is marked by
options: a distinct wet season in summer and a long dry season
questions.explanation: Rainfall is seasonal, decreasing poleward, with a long dry season.

questions.stem: Which of the following gases is a major greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour trap outgoing heat.

questions.stem: Which of the following human activities contributes most directly to global warming?
questions.explanation: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: A likely effect of global warming on low-lying coastal cities such as Lagos is
options: increased flooding due to rising sea level
questions.explanation: Thermal expansion and melting ice raise sea level.

questions.stem: The international agreement adopted in 2015 under which countries set targets to limit global temperature rise to well below 2 degrees C is the
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep warming well below 2 degrees C and pursue 1.5 degrees C.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a renewable environmental resource?
questions.explanation: Forests can regenerate if well managed; minerals are exhaustible.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an environmental resource used for generating hydro-electric power?
questions.explanation: Rivers provide water power, e.g. at Kainji on the Niger.

questions.stem: Solar energy is particularly suitable for northern Nigeria because the area has
options: long hours of sunshine and few cloudy days for much of the year
questions.explanation: High insolation and a long dry season favour solar power.

questions.stem: A resource is said to be exhaustible when
options: it can be used for many purposes
it cannot be replaced within a human time scale once used
it increases as it is used
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels and minerals are exhaustible.

questions.stem: The gradual spread of desert-like conditions into semi-arid lands is called
questions.explanation: Desertification affects northern Nigeria and the Sahel.

questions.stem: Gully erosion is a serious environmental problem in parts of
options: south-eastern Nigeria, such as Anambra State
questions.explanation: Loose sandy soils, heavy rainfall and poor land use cause severe gullies in the south-east.

questions.stem: Oil spillage in the Niger Delta leads mainly to
options: pollution of farmland and water bodies, destroying fisheries
questions.explanation: Spills poison soil and water and damage livelihoods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a natural environmental hazard?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes are natural; the others are human-made problems.

questions.stem: Blocked drainage channels in cities such as Lagos contribute to
questions.explanation: Refuse in drains prevents runoff and causes floods.

questions.stem: The planting of trees on land that has not had forest cover for a long time or where forest has been cleared is part of
questions.explanation: Tree planting checks erosion and desertification.

questions.stem: The Great Green Wall initiative in Africa aims mainly to
options: check desertification across the Sahel by restoring vegetation
questions.explanation: It restores degraded land along the southern edge of the Sahara.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods conserves soil on steep farmland?
options: Ploughing up and down the slope
questions.explanation: Terraces and contour ridges slow runoff and reduce erosion.

questions.stem: The official counting of all the people in a country at a particular time is called
questions.explanation: A census collects demographic data on the whole population.

questions.stem: A country with 2,500,000 people living in an area of 5,000 square kilometres has a population density of
If the birth rate of a country is 38 per thousand and the death rate is 12 per thousand, the rate of natural increase is
questions.explanation: 38 - 12 = 26 per thousand = 2.6 per cent.

questions.stem: A population pyramid with a broad base and a narrow top indicates
options: equal numbers in every age group
high birth rates and a youthful population
questions.explanation: Many young dependants is typical of developing countries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pull factor in rural-urban migration?
options: Lack of social amenities in the village
Better job opportunities in the city
questions.explanation: Pull factors attract migrants to the destination; push factors drive them from the source.

questions.stem: The idea that population grows faster than food supply, leading to famine, war and disease as checks, was put forward by
questions.explanation: Malthus (1798) argued population grows geometrically and food arithmetically.

questions.stem: A country's population is 45 per cent dependants and 55 per cent of working age. Its dependency ratio is about
questions.explanation: 45/55 x 100 = 81.8, about 82 dependants per 100 workers.

questions.stem: Which of the following areas of the world has a very low population density?
questions.explanation: Harsh dry conditions discourage settlement in the Sahara.

questions.stem: A town with a population of 1,200,000 grows at 3 per cent per annum. Its population after one year will be
A settlement in which houses are grouped closely together is said to be
questions.explanation: Nucleated settlements cluster around a centre.

questions.stem: A settlement whose houses stretch along a road, river or railway is
questions.explanation: Linear (ribbon) settlements follow lines of communication.

questions.stem: The 'site' of a settlement refers to
options: its position relative to surrounding areas
the actual land on which it is built
questions.explanation: Situation is its location relative to the surrounding region.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of an urban settlement?
questions.explanation: Towns provide administrative, commercial, industrial and service functions.

questions.stem: When two or more expanding towns merge to form one continuous urban area, it is called
questions.explanation: Conurbations form through urban sprawl.

questions.stem: Two common results of the rapid growth of West African cities are
questions.explanation: Rapid urban growth causes congestion, slums and pressure on services.

questions.stem: A city that is very much larger than the next largest city in a country and dominates its economy is
questions.explanation: Primate cities dominate the urban hierarchy.

questions.stem: Rural settlements in the Sahel often grow near
questions.explanation: Water supply is a key factor in siting settlements in dry areas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the dispersed settlement pattern in some rural areas?
options: Farmers live on their own scattered farmlands
Shortage of water except at a few points
questions.explanation: Dispersal occurs where water is widely available and people live on their farms.

questions.stem: The Suez Canal links the
options: Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
Gulf of Guinea and Indian Ocean
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.stem: Which mode of transport is most suitable for carrying crude oil and natural gas over long distances on land?
questions.explanation: Pipelines move liquids and gases cheaply and continuously.

questions.stem: Air transport is most suitable for
options: carrying heavy cement in large volumes
carrying perishable and high-value goods quickly
questions.explanation: Air is fast but expensive.

questions.stem: The Trans-Siberian Railway links
questions.explanation: It crosses Russia from Moscow to the Pacific port of Vladivostok.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of water transport?
options: It is the most expensive per tonne
It is slow and limited to navigable routes
questions.explanation: Water transport is cheap for bulk but slow and route-restricted.

questions.stem: The Panama Canal is important because it
options: links the Red Sea and the Mediterranean
connects the Great Lakes to the Atlantic
shortens the sea route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans
joins the Niger and Benue rivers
questions.explanation: Ships avoid the long voyage round South America.

questions.stem: Road transport is the most widely used mode of transport in West Africa mainly because
options: it is the cheapest for heavy bulk over long distances
it offers door-to-door service and reaches most settlements
questions.explanation: Flexibility and accessibility make roads dominant.

questions.stem: The processing of raw materials into finished goods is
questions.explanation: Mining and farming are primary; services are tertiary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary industry?
questions.explanation: Primary industries extract natural resources.

questions.stem: Industries whose raw materials lose much weight during processing tend to be located
options: near the source of raw materials
questions.explanation: Weight-losing industries, such as cement and sugar, locate near raw materials to cut transport costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors favours the location of industries in large cities?
options: Availability of a large market and labour
questions.explanation: Market, labour, services and transport attract industry to cities.

questions.stem: Industries that are not tied to any particular raw material or market and can locate in many places are described as
questions.explanation: Footloose industries, e.g. electronics assembly, have flexible locations.

questions.stem: The Ruhr region of Germany developed as a major industrial area mainly because of
options: large deposits of coal and good river transport
questions.explanation: Coal and the Rhine waterway supported its iron and steel industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of industrialisation in developing countries?
questions.explanation: Unreliable power raises costs and limits production.

questions.stem: The exchange of goods and services between countries is
questions.explanation: International trade crosses national boundaries.

questions.stem: When the value of a country's visible exports exceeds that of its visible imports, it has
questions.explanation: Balance of trade compares visible exports and imports.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a barrier to international trade?
questions.explanation: Tariffs and quotas restrict trade.

questions.stem: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) aims to
options: create a single market for goods and services across Africa
ban all imports from outside Africa
questions.explanation: AfCFTA seeks to reduce tariffs and boost intra-African trade.

questions.stem: The headquarters (secretariat) of the AfCFTA is located in
questions.explanation: The AfCFTA Secretariat is in Accra, Ghana; the African Union headquarters is in Addis Ababa.

questions.stem: Many West African countries suffer from poor terms of trade mainly because they
options: export mostly raw materials whose prices are low and unstable
questions.explanation: Primary commodity prices fluctuate and are low relative to manufactured imports.

questions.stem: Travelling to places for pleasure, leisure or recreation is
questions.explanation: Tourism involves temporary travel for leisure, business or culture.

questions.stem: Tourism benefits a host country mainly by
questions.explanation: Tourism generates income and jobs.

questions.stem: A possible harmful consequence of mass tourism in a fragile area such as a coral reef or game reserve is
options: pollution and damage to the environment
questions.explanation: Large numbers of visitors may damage ecosystems.

questions.stem: Ecotourism refers to tourism that
options: focuses on natural areas and promotes conservation and local benefit
questions.explanation: Ecotourism is responsible travel to natural areas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor that encourages the growth of tourism in a country?
questions.explanation: Insecurity discourages tourists.

questions.stem: Nigeria shares its western boundary with
questions.explanation: Benin is west; Niger north; Chad north-east; Cameroon east.

questions.stem: Nigeria is made up of
options: 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states plus the FCT, Abuja.

questions.stem: Nigeria lies approximately between latitudes
questions.explanation: Nigeria lies roughly between 4 and 14 degrees N and 3 and 15 degrees E.

questions.stem: The number of local government areas in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The constitution lists 774 local government areas.

questions.stem: The rivers Niger and Benue meet at
questions.explanation: The confluence is at Lokoja, Kogi State.

questions.stem: The highest point in Nigeria, Chappal Waddi, is located in
questions.explanation: Chappal Waddi (about 2,419 m) is in the Gotel Mountains of Taraba State, near the Cameroon border.

questions.stem: The dry, dusty north-east trade wind that blows over Nigeria from about November to February is
questions.explanation: The Harmattan comes from the Sahara (tropical continental air mass).

questions.stem: The vegetation belt found along the coast of the Niger Delta is
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in brackish coastal swamps.

questions.stem: Annual rainfall in Nigeria generally
options: increases from the south to the north
decreases from the south to the north
questions.explanation: The coast receives the most rain; amounts decrease northwards.

questions.stem: The Jos Plateau has a cooler climate than surrounding lowlands mainly because of its
questions.explanation: Temperature falls with altitude.

questions.stem: Which part of Nigeria has one of the highest population densities?
options: The desert fringe of the Chad basin
questions.explanation: Lagos is Nigeria's largest urban agglomeration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of Nigeria's rapid population growth?
options: Pressure on schools, housing and health facilities
questions.explanation: Rapid growth strains infrastructure and services.

questions.stem: Crude oil was first discovered in commercial quantities in Nigeria at
questions.explanation: Oil was found at Oloibiri (now Bayelsa State) in 1956.

questions.stem: Tin and columbite are mined mainly on
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau is Nigeria's main tin and columbite area.

questions.stem: Iron ore for the Ajaokuta steel project is found at
questions.explanation: Itakpe in Kogi State has iron ore deposits; Ewekoro and Nkalagu have limestone.

questions.stem: Which of the following Nigerian dams is on the River Niger?
questions.explanation: Kainji (and Jebba) are on the Niger; Shiroro is on the Kaduna River.

questions.stem: Bitumen deposits in Nigeria are found mainly in
questions.explanation: Nigeria's bitumen belt lies mainly in Ondo State, extending into Ogun, Edo and Lagos.

questions.stem: Cocoa is grown mainly in
questions.explanation: Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Oyo and Ekiti States are major cocoa producers; Cross River also grows cocoa.

questions.stem: Groundnuts are grown mainly in the
options: northern parts of Nigeria, e.g. Kano and Katsina
questions.explanation: Light sandy soils and moderate rainfall in the north suit groundnuts.

questions.stem: The Bakolori Irrigation Project is located in
options: Zamfara State, in the Sokoto-Rima basin
questions.explanation: Bakolori Dam on the Sokoto (Rima) River supplies irrigation in the north-west.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem facing agriculture in Nigeria?
options: Poor storage facilities leading to post-harvest losses
questions.explanation: Lack of storage and processing causes large losses.

questions.stem: Nomadic cattle herding is common in northern Nigeria mainly because
options: the forests provide shade all year
the area is relatively free from the tsetse fly and has grassland
questions.explanation: Tsetse flies, which spread trypanosomiasis, are more common in the humid south.

questions.stem: The standard-gauge railway commissioned in 2021 links Lagos with
questions.explanation: The Lagos-Ibadan standard-gauge line was commissioned in 2021.

questions.stem: Onne, Apapa and Tin Can Island are
options: inland dry ports in northern Nigeria
questions.explanation: Onne (Rivers State) is a major port; others include Apapa, Tin Can Island and Lekki.

questions.stem: Inland waterway transport in Nigeria is limited mainly because
options: roads are always cheaper for bulk goods
rivers have seasonal fluctuations in water level and obstacles such as sandbars
questions.explanation: Low water in the dry season and silting hinder navigation.

questions.stem: The body that regulates the telecommunications industry in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The NCC regulates telecoms operators.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of the growth of mobile telephone and internet services in Nigeria?
options: Faster business transactions and access to information
An end to postal services worldwide
questions.explanation: ICT growth supports commerce, banking and education.

questions.stem: A large cement factory at Obajana is located in
questions.explanation: Obajana in Kogi State has extensive limestone and one of Africa's largest cement plants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the concentration of industries in Lagos?
options: Port facilities and a large market
questions.explanation: Lagos has ports, capital, labour and the largest consumer market.

questions.stem: Which of the following industries is raw-material oriented in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cement is weight-losing, so plants locate near limestone deposits.

questions.stem: Nigeria's leading export by value is
questions.explanation: Petroleum dominates Nigeria's export earnings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of Nigeria's foreign trade?
options: Over-dependence on a single export commodity
questions.explanation: Dependence on oil exposes the economy to price swings.

questions.stem: The Yankari Game Reserve, noted for the Wikki Warm Spring, is in
questions.explanation: Yankari is in Bauchi State.

questions.stem: The Argungu Fishing Festival is held in
questions.explanation: Argungu is in Kebbi State.

questions.topic: Issues on development and environmental concerns in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following is a major environmental concern in the Niger Delta?
questions.explanation: Gas flaring pollutes air and contributes to climate change.

questions.topic: Issues on development and environmental concerns in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following is a likely cause of the severe floods experienced in many Nigerian states in recent years?
options: Volcanic eruptions on the Jos Plateau
Heavy rainfall combined with the release of water from dams and blocked drainage
questions.explanation: Intense rains, dam releases and poor drainage caused major floods, e.g. in 2012 and 2022.

questions.stem: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in 1975 by the Treaty of
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was founded by the Treaty of Lagos on 28 May 1975.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the ECOWAS Commission is in
questions.explanation: The Commission is located in Abuja, Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of ECOWAS?
questions.explanation: Cameroon belongs to the Central African economic community (ECCAS/CEMAC), not ECOWAS.

questions.stem: One of the main objectives of ECOWAS is to
options: create a single army to conquer neighbours
promote economic integration and free movement of people and goods among member states
questions.explanation: ECOWAS protocols include free movement and trade liberalisation.

questions.stem: The Bakassi Peninsula, which was the subject of a boundary dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon, was awarded to Cameroon by
questions.explanation: The ICJ ruled in 2002; the handover was completed in 2008.

questions.stem: The movement of Abuja as Nigeria's capital from Lagos was officially done in
questions.explanation: Abuja was chosen in 1976 and became the capital in December 1991.

questions.stem: The first stage in carrying out geographical field work is
options: planning, including choosing the topic and objectives
questions.explanation: Field work begins with planning, then reconnaissance, data collection, analysis and reporting.

questions.stem: A preliminary visit to the study area before the actual field work is called
questions.explanation: Reconnaissance helps the researcher to plan the main study.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary source of data in field work?
questions.explanation: Primary data are collected first-hand.

questions.stem: An instrument used in field work to measure the gradient of a slope is
questions.explanation: Clinometers measure slope angles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a precaution students should take during field work?
options: Obtaining permission from local authorities and observing safety rules
Working alone in unfamiliar places at night
Taking samples from private farms without consent
questions.explanation: Permission and safety are essential in field work.

questions.stem:
A topographical map has a scale of 1:50,000.
(a) Express the scale as a statement scale. [2 marks]
(b) A motorable road measures 7.2 cm on the map. Calculate its length on the ground in kilometres. [3 marks]
(c) Two spot heights on the road are 520 m and 280 m above sea level and are 3.6 km apart. Calculate the average gradient between them. [4 marks]
(d) Describe three methods of showing relief on topographical maps. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) 1 cm represents 0.5 km (or 2 cm represent 1 km)
1 mark: (b) 7.2 x 50,000 = 360,000 cm
2 marks: (b) = 3.6 km
1 mark: (c) Vertical interval = 520 - 280 = 240 m
1 mark: (c) Horizontal equivalent = 3.6 km = 3,600 m
2 marks: (c) Gradient = 240/3,600 = 1 in 15
2 marks: (d) Contours: lines joining places of equal height above sea level
2 marks: (d) Spot heights and trigonometrical stations: exact heights marked by dots or triangles
2 marks: (d) Layer tinting, hachures or hill shading: colours or strokes showing height and steepness
questions.explanation: 1:50,000 means 1 cm to 0.5 km. 7.2 cm x 0.5 = 3.6 km. Gradient = 240 m over 3,600 m = 1 in 15. Relief is shown by contours, spot heights/trigonometrical stations, and layer tints, hachures or hill shading.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a Geographic Information System (GIS)? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four components of GIS. [8 marks]
(c) State four uses of GIS. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) A computer-based system for capturing, storing, analysing, managing and displaying spatially referenced (geographic) data
2 marks: (b) Hardware: computers, GPS receivers, scanners, printers
2 marks: (b) Software: programs for storing, analysing and displaying data
2 marks: (b) Data: spatial (location) data and attribute data, in vector or raster form
2 marks: (b) People and methods: trained users and procedures for analysis
1 mark: (c) Urban and regional planning
1 mark: (c) Environmental monitoring, e.g. flooding and deforestation
1 mark: (c) Transport route planning and navigation
1 mark: (c) Census mapping, election planning, agriculture or disaster management
questions.explanation: GIS is a computer system for handling geographic data. It comprises hardware, software, data and people/methods. It supports planning, environmental monitoring, transport, census and disaster management.

questions.stem:
The table shows crop output (in thousand tonnes) in a district: maize 450, yam 300, cassava 600, rice 150.
(a) Calculate the angle of each sector for a pie chart. [8 marks]
(b) State three advantages of a pie chart. [3 marks]
(c) State two disadvantages of a pie chart. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Total = 1,500 thousand tonnes
2 marks: (a) Maize: 450/1,500 x 360 = 108 degrees
2 marks: (a) Yam: 300/1,500 x 360 = 72 degrees
2 marks: (a) Cassava: 600/1,500 x 360 = 144 degrees
1 mark: (a) Rice: 150/1,500 x 360 = 36 degrees
1 mark: (b) It shows clearly the proportion of each part to the whole
1 mark: (b) It is easy to draw and read
1 mark: (b) It is visually attractive for comparison
2 marks: (c) Small values are hard to show and compare when sectors are tiny
2 marks: (c) Exact values cannot be read directly unless written on the chart; too many components make it cluttered
questions.explanation: Total 1,500; angles: maize 108, yam 72, cassava 144, rice 36 degrees (sum 360). Pie charts show proportions clearly and are easy to read, but small sectors and exact values are hard to interpret.

questions.stem:
(a) A football match in Lagos (3 degrees E) starts at 10.00 a.m. local time. Calculate the local time in a city on longitude 120 degrees E when the match starts. [5 marks]
(b) Explain four effects of the rotation of the earth. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Longitude difference = 120 - 3 = 117 degrees
2 marks: (a) Time difference = 117 x 4 minutes = 468 minutes = 7 hours 48 minutes
2 marks: (a) City is east, so ahead: 10.00 a.m. + 7 h 48 min = 5.48 p.m.
3 marks: (b) Day and night occur as each part of the earth turns towards and away from the sun
3 marks: (b) Difference in time between places on different longitudes (1 degree = 4 minutes)
2 marks: (b) Deflection of winds and ocean currents (Coriolis force): to the right in the northern and left in the southern hemisphere
2 marks: (b) Daily rise and fall of tides and apparent movement of the sun from east to west
questions.explanation: 117 degrees x 4 min = 7 h 48 min; the city is ahead, so 5.48 p.m. Rotation causes day and night, time differences, deflection of winds and currents, and the apparent daily movement of the sun and tides.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how each of the following types of rock is formed and give one example of each: (i) igneous; (ii) sedimentary; (iii) metamorphic. [9 marks]
(b) State three economic uses of rocks in Nigeria. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Igneous: formed by cooling and solidification of magma (intrusive) or lava (extrusive), e.g. granite or basalt
3 marks: (a)(ii) Sedimentary: formed by deposition and compaction of sediments, organic remains or chemical precipitates in layers, e.g. sandstone, limestone, coal
3 marks: (a)(iii) Metamorphic: formed when existing rocks are changed by great heat and/or pressure, e.g. marble from limestone, slate from shale
2 marks: (b) Limestone for cement manufacture, e.g. at Ewekoro and Obajana
2 marks: (b) Granite and other hard rocks quarried for building and road construction
2 marks: (b) Coal as fuel; rocks as sources of minerals such as tin; tourist attractions such as Olumo Rock
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava (granite, basalt); sedimentary rocks from compacted layered sediments (sandstone, limestone, coal); metamorphic rocks from heat and pressure on existing rocks (marble, slate). In Nigeria rocks supply cement raw material, construction stone, fuel and minerals, and attract tourists.

questions.stem:
(a) With the aid of a description, explain how a rift valley is formed. [7 marks]
(b) Name one example of a rift valley. [2 marks]
(c) State three ways in which tectonic landforms are useful to man. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Tension (pulling apart) or compression in the earth's crust produces two roughly parallel faults
3 marks: (a) Under tension, the central block between the faults sinks; or under compression the side blocks are pushed up over the central block
2 marks: (a) The result is a long, narrow, steep-sided valley with fault scarps on both sides
2 marks: (b) The East African (Great) Rift Valley or the Rhine Rift Valley
2 marks: (c) Rift valleys and fold mountains attract tourists
2 marks: (c) Rift valley lakes provide water, fish and transport
2 marks: (c) Volcanic areas give fertile soils, minerals and geothermal energy; mountains influence rainfall
questions.explanation: Parallel faults develop under tension or compression; the central block sinks (or the sides rise), forming a steep-sided rift valley such as the East African Rift. Such landforms support tourism, lakes for fishing and water, fertile volcanic soils, minerals and geothermal energy.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the formation of the following features in the lower course of a river: (i) meander; (ii) ox-bow lake; (iii) delta. [12 marks]
(b) State three ways in which rivers are useful to man. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) The river swings in loops; erosion is greatest on the outer (concave) bank, forming river cliffs
2 marks: (a)(i) Deposition on the inner (convex) bank forms slip-off slopes, increasing the loop
2 marks: (a)(ii) Continued erosion narrows the neck of a meander until the river breaks through during a flood
2 marks: (a)(ii) Deposition seals off the old loop, leaving a crescent-shaped ox-bow lake
2 marks: (a)(iii) Where a river enters a calm sea or lake, its speed falls and it deposits its load
2 marks: (a)(iii) Deposits build up, the river divides into distributaries, forming a delta, e.g. the Niger Delta
1 mark: (b) Water supply for domestic use and irrigation
1 mark: (b) Fishing and transport
1 mark: (b) Hydro-electric power generation
questions.explanation: Meanders grow by outer-bank erosion and inner-bank deposition; when the neck is cut through, the abandoned loop becomes an ox-bow lake. Deltas form where rivers deposit their load on entering calm water, dividing into distributaries. Rivers supply water, fish, transport and power.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the instrument used to measure each of the following weather elements and state the unit of measurement: (i) rainfall; (ii) temperature; (iii) atmospheric pressure; (iv) wind speed; (v) relative humidity. [10 marks]
(b) Explain two factors to consider when siting a weather station. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Rain gauge; millimetres
2 marks: (a)(ii) Thermometer (e.g. Six's maximum and minimum thermometer); degrees Celsius
2 marks: (a)(iii) Barometer; millibars (hectopascals)
2 marks: (a)(iv) Anemometer; kilometres per hour, metres per second or knots
2 marks: (a)(v) Hygrometer (wet-and-dry bulb thermometer); per cent
3 marks: (b) Open place away from tall buildings and trees that may shelter instruments or cast shadows
2 marks: (b) Level, secure and accessible ground, protected from interference
questions.explanation: Rain gauge (mm), thermometer (degrees C), barometer (mb/hPa), anemometer (km/h or knots) and hygrometer (per cent). A station should be in an open, level, secure place away from buildings and trees.

questions.stem:
The data below are for a station in West Africa.
Temperature (degrees C), Jan to Dec: 27, 28, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 24, 25, 26, 27, 27
Rainfall (mm), Jan to Dec: 10, 25, 70, 120, 160, 210, 230, 250, 200, 110, 30, 5
(a) Calculate: (i) the annual range of temperature; (ii) the mean annual temperature; (iii) the total annual rainfall. [6 marks]
(b) Name the wettest and the driest months. [2 marks]
(c) Describe the climate of the station as shown by the data. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) 28 - 24 = 4 degrees C
2 marks: (a)(ii) 314 / 12 = 26.2 degrees C (approximately)
2 marks: (a)(iii) 1,420 mm
1 mark: (b) Wettest month: August (250 mm)
1 mark: (b) Driest month: December (5 mm)
2 marks: (c) High temperatures throughout the year with a small annual range
2 marks: (c) Rainfall is seasonal, with a wet season from about April to October
2 marks: (c) A dry season from about November to March
1 mark: (c) It is a tropical (Guinea savanna / tropical continental) type of climate in the northern hemisphere
questions.explanation: Range 4 degrees C; mean about 26.2 degrees C; total 1,420 mm. Wettest August, driest December. Hot all year with a small range, a wet season April-October and a dry season November-March: a tropical wet-and-dry climate of the northern hemisphere.

questions.stem:
(a) What is climate change? [3 marks]
(b) Explain three causes of climate change. [6 marks]
(c) State three effects of climate change on Nigeria. [3 marks]
(d) Suggest three ways of reducing the effects of climate change. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) A long-term change in the average weather conditions (temperature, rainfall, winds) of a place or the earth as a whole
2 marks: (b) Burning of fossil fuels releasing carbon dioxide
2 marks: (b) Deforestation, which reduces the absorption of carbon dioxide
2 marks: (b) Gas flaring, agriculture and waste releasing methane and other greenhouse gases
1 mark: (c) Increased desertification and drought in the north
1 mark: (c) Coastal flooding and erosion due to rising sea level
1 mark: (c) Irregular rainfall affecting crop yields and food security
1 mark: (d) Afforestation and reforestation
1 mark: (d) Use of renewable energy such as solar and wind
1 mark: (d) Ending gas flaring and improving energy efficiency
questions.explanation: Climate change is long-term change in average weather patterns, driven mainly by greenhouse gases from fossil fuels, deforestation and gas flaring. Nigeria faces desertification, coastal flooding and irregular rainfall; responses include tree planting, renewable energy and ending gas flaring.

questions.stem:
(a) What is desertification? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four causes of desertification in West Africa. [8 marks]
(c) Describe three effects of desertification. [6 marks]
(d) Suggest three measures to control desertification. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) The degradation of land in arid and semi-arid areas into desert-like conditions due to climatic variations and human activities
2 marks: (b) Overgrazing by large herds of livestock
2 marks: (b) Deforestation for fuelwood and farmland
2 marks: (b) Bush burning and poor farming practices such as continuous cropping
2 marks: (b) Prolonged drought and low, unreliable rainfall
2 marks: (c) Loss of farmland and reduced crop yields, causing food shortages
2 marks: (c) Migration of people and herders southwards, sometimes leading to conflict
2 marks: (c) Drying up of water sources and loss of vegetation and wildlife
1 mark: (d) Planting shelter belts and trees (e.g. the Great Green Wall)
1 mark: (d) Controlled grazing and ranching
1 mark: (d) Use of alternative energy to reduce fuelwood cutting
questions.explanation: Desertification is land degradation in drylands. It is caused by overgrazing, deforestation, bush burning and drought, and leads to food shortages, migration and conflict, and loss of water and vegetation. It can be checked by shelter belts, controlled grazing and alternative fuels.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five factors that influence the distribution of population in the world. [15 marks]
(b) State five problems associated with overpopulation. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Climate: moderate climates attract people; very hot, cold or dry areas are sparsely populated
3 marks: (a) Relief: lowlands and plains are densely settled; rugged mountains are sparsely settled
3 marks: (a) Soils: fertile soils (e.g. river valleys and deltas) support dense farming populations
3 marks: (a) Mineral and other resources attract people, e.g. mining towns
3 marks: (a) Economic, political and historical factors: industry, trade, government policy and security
1 mark: (b) Unemployment
1 mark: (b) Housing shortages and slums
1 mark: (b) Pressure on food supply
1 mark: (b) Overstretched social amenities
1 mark: (b) Environmental degradation and crime
questions.explanation: Population is dense where climate is moderate, land is low and fertile, resources are found and economic opportunities and security exist; it is sparse in deserts, mountains and poor soils. Overpopulation causes unemployment, housing shortages, food pressure, strained services and environmental problems.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between rural and urban settlements. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four factors that influence the siting of settlements. [8 marks]
(c) Describe three problems of urban centres in West Africa and suggest a solution to each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Rural settlements are small; urban settlements are large in population and area
2 marks: (a) Rural people are mainly engaged in primary activities such as farming; urban people in secondary and tertiary activities
2 marks: (a) Urban areas have more social amenities and denser buildings than rural areas
2 marks: (b) Water supply
2 marks: (b) Relief and drainage: well-drained, flat or gently sloping land
2 marks: (b) Defence and security, e.g. hilltops
2 marks: (b) Fertile soils, route centres and mineral resources
2 marks: (c) Traffic congestion: build more roads and mass transit
2 marks: (c) Slums and housing shortages: provide affordable housing and urban renewal
2 marks: (c) Poor waste disposal and flooding: improve sanitation and drainage
questions.explanation: Rural settlements are small and agricultural; urban ones are large, non-agricultural and better served. Sites are chosen for water, good drainage, defence, fertile soil and routes. Urban congestion, slums and waste/flooding call for transit, housing schemes and better sanitation and drainage.

questions.stem:
(a) Compare road and rail transport under the following headings: (i) cost of construction; (ii) flexibility; (iii) carrying capacity; (iv) speed over long distances. [12 marks]
(b) State four problems of transportation in West Africa. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Roads are generally cheaper to construct and maintain; railways are costly
3 marks: (a)(ii) Roads offer door-to-door service and reach most settlements; rail follows fixed tracks and stations
3 marks: (a)(iii) Rail carries heavier and bulkier loads more cheaply per tonne
3 marks: (a)(iv) Rail can be faster and less affected by congestion over long distances; roads suffer delays
2 marks: (b) Poor maintenance of roads and railways
2 marks: (b) Inadequate funding and capital
2 marks: (b) Seasonal flooding and difficult terrain
2 marks: (b) Insecurity, congestion and accidents
questions.explanation: Roads are cheaper and more flexible; railways carry bulk more cheaply and can be faster over long distances. West African transport suffers from poor maintenance, lack of funds, flooding and terrain, insecurity, congestion and accidents.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five factors that influence the location of manufacturing industries. [15 marks]
(b) State five contributions of manufacturing industries to the economy of a country. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Raw materials: weight-losing industries locate near raw materials, e.g. cement near limestone
3 marks: (a) Market: industries making perishable or bulky finished goods locate near consumers
3 marks: (a) Power supply: reliable electricity or fuel is essential
3 marks: (a) Labour: availability of skilled and unskilled workers
3 marks: (a) Transport, capital and government policy
1 mark: (b) Provides employment
1 mark: (b) Earns foreign exchange through exports
1 mark: (b) Saves foreign exchange through import substitution
1 mark: (b) Provides revenue for government
1 mark: (b) Promotes development of infrastructure and urbanisation
questions.explanation: Industries are located by raw materials, markets, power, labour, transport, capital and government policy. They provide jobs, foreign exchange, import substitution, revenue and infrastructure.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five factors that encourage tourism in a country. [10 marks]
(b) Discuss five benefits of tourism to the economy of a country. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Attractive physical features such as beaches, waterfalls, mountains and wildlife
2 marks: (a) Rich cultural heritage and festivals
2 marks: (a) Political stability and security
2 marks: (a) Good transport, accommodation and communication facilities
2 marks: (a) Favourable climate and effective publicity
2 marks: (b) Earns foreign exchange
2 marks: (b) Creates jobs for guides, hotel workers and craftsmen
2 marks: (b) Encourages development of infrastructure
2 marks: (b) Provides revenue for government
2 marks: (b) Promotes local crafts, cultural exchange and international understanding
questions.explanation: Tourism grows where there are scenic attractions, culture and festivals, security, good infrastructure, favourable climate and publicity. It earns foreign exchange, creates jobs, improves infrastructure, raises revenue and promotes crafts and cultural exchange.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the relief of Nigeria under four headings. [12 marks]
(b) Explain four ways in which relief influences human activities in Nigeria. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Coastal lowlands and the Niger Delta: low-lying, swampy, with creeks and lagoons
3 marks: (a) Plains and river basins: Niger-Benue trough, Sokoto plains, Chad basin
3 marks: (a) Plateaux and uplands: Jos Plateau, Western/Yoruba uplands, Udi Plateau
3 marks: (a) Eastern highlands along the Cameroon border: Obudu, Mambilla, Adamawa highlands, with Chappal Waddi the highest point
2 marks: (b) Lowlands and plains favour farming and dense settlement
2 marks: (b) Highlands like Jos and Obudu have cool climates favouring tourism and livestock
2 marks: (b) Rugged relief makes road and rail construction difficult and expensive
2 marks: (b) Rivers falling from uplands provide hydro-electric power sites, e.g. Kainji and Shiroro
questions.explanation: Nigeria has coastal lowlands and the Delta, interior plains and basins, central and western plateaux, and eastern highlands. Relief affects settlement and farming, encourages tourism and ranching on cool highlands, raises transport costs and provides HEP sites.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five problems facing agriculture in Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) Suggest five ways in which agricultural production in Nigeria can be improved. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Use of crude tools and traditional methods
2 marks: (a) Inadequate credit and capital for farmers
2 marks: (a) Poor storage, processing and transport facilities causing post-harvest losses
2 marks: (a) Pests, diseases, soil erosion and irregular rainfall
2 marks: (a) Land tenure problems and insecurity in farming areas
2 marks: (b) Mechanisation and use of improved seeds and fertilizers
2 marks: (b) Provision of loans and subsidies through agricultural banks
2 marks: (b) Building storage, processing facilities and rural roads
2 marks: (b) Expanding irrigation and extension services
2 marks: (b) Land reform and improved security for farmers
questions.explanation: Nigerian agriculture is held back by crude tools, poor credit, storage and transport, pests and erratic rainfall, land tenure and insecurity. Improvements include mechanisation and improved inputs, credit, storage and roads, irrigation and extension, land reform and security.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the distribution of the petroleum industry in Nigeria. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four contributions of the petroleum industry to the Nigerian economy. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three problems associated with the petroleum industry in Nigeria. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Crude oil and gas are produced mainly in the Niger Delta: Rivers, Bayelsa, Delta and Akwa Ibom States, both onshore and offshore
2 marks: (a) Refineries have been located at Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna, and a large private refinery at Lekki near Lagos
2 marks: (a) Pipelines and export terminals link the fields with refineries, depots and ports such as Bonny and Forcados
2 marks: (b) Main source of foreign exchange
2 marks: (b) Major source of government revenue
2 marks: (b) Provides employment and raw materials for petrochemical industries
2 marks: (b) Supplies fuel and energy for transport and industry
2 marks: (c) Oil spillage and gas flaring pollute land, water and air
2 marks: (c) Pipeline vandalism, theft and illegal refining
2 marks: (c) Over-dependence on oil exposes the economy to fluctuating world prices
questions.explanation: Oil and gas come mainly from the Niger Delta states, onshore and offshore, with refineries at Port Harcourt, Warri, Kaduna and Lekki and terminals such as Bonny and Forcados. Petroleum earns most foreign exchange and revenue, creates jobs and supplies energy, but causes pollution, attracts vandalism and makes the economy vulnerable to price swings.

questions.stem:
(a) State five objectives of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). [10 marks]
(b) Explain five problems that hinder the achievement of the objectives of ECOWAS. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) To promote economic co-operation and integration among member states
2 marks: (a) To ensure free movement of people, goods and services
2 marks: (a) To remove tariffs and other barriers to trade among members
2 marks: (a) To develop regional infrastructure such as roads and telecommunications
2 marks: (a) To promote peace, security and stability in the region
2 marks: (b) Political instability and military coups in some member states
2 marks: (b) Different currencies and monetary systems
2 marks: (b) Poor transport and communication links between members
2 marks: (b) Similar products (mostly primary goods), which limit trade among members
2 marks: (b) Poor implementation of protocols, border restrictions and inadequate funding
questions.explanation: ECOWAS seeks economic integration, free movement, tariff removal, regional infrastructure and peace. It is hindered by instability and coups, multiple currencies, poor links, similar exports, and weak implementation and funding.
